findings.how_to_check: Tabulate link provenance and profile creation dates relative to census attachment dates. Compare agreement rates across name frequency deciles and race/nativity groups. To validate accuracy, conduct a blinded hand-audit of raw census images.
findings.suggested_fix: Frame this exhibit strictly as descriptive agreement with a FamilySearch-linked genealogical reference, not as accuracy or independent validation. For any claim of accuracy, evaluate on an independently sampled, hand-verified ground-truth dataset.
findings.title: FamilySearch-linked profile names are an endogenous benchmark, not an independent validation of transcription accuracy
findings.what_the_code_does: Census records are linked to FamilySearch profiles via unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1940.dta, and each transcription source (Ancestry, FamilySearch census index, ML) is scored against the profile's name. Although the header and markdown note acknowledge that users attach records through FamilySearch's index and may copy names from it, the analysis is intended for the appendix as a benchmark (tab:transcription_accuracy).
findings.why_it_matters: FamilySearch profile names are largely created and curated by genealogists who discover and attach 1940 census records using FamilySearch's transcription and search algorithms. This generates mechanical agreement favoring FamilySearch. Furthermore, selection into being attached to a profile strongly correlates with name legibility, commonness, and Anglo-American ethnicity, meaning agreement rates within this linked subsample cannot measure transcription accuracy in the general census population.

findings.title: The profile name analysis is omitted from the replication master and depends on an unconfigured, hardcoded E: drive path
findings.what_the_code_does: MATCHING/profile_names_build.do hardcodes local prof "E:/multigen_CM/DATA/INTERMEDIATE" and do "D:/repos/fixing_transcription_errors/replication/config.do", but replication/config.do defines no global for the E: drive. Furthermore, neither replication/run_machineA.do nor MATCHING/_matching_master_dofile.do preflights these inputs or invokes profile_names_build.do and profile_names_score.do.
findings.why_it_matters: The replication pipeline cannot build profile_names.dta or generate profile_names.md. Any external replicator or run on Machine B fails immediately when attempting to confirm or read all_individual_info*.dta on the non-existent E: path.

findings.how_to_check: In profile_names_build.do before drop if _mh | _mu, compute distinct histid if _mh, distinct unique_ID if _mu, and count if _mh & _mu. Compare the distinct ID counts to n_xmh and n_xmu.
findings.suggested_fix: Store and report distinct counts of affected histids and unique_IDs, or label the rows explicitly as crosswalk pairs/rows dropped, and report the net union of removed census records.
findings.title: The sample selection table reports ambiguous crosswalk row counts as numbers of dropped records
findings.what_the_code_does: In MATCHING/profile_names_build.do, lines 94-98 calculate n_xmh = r(N) from count if _mh and n_xmu = r(N) from count if _mu, where _mh flags histids appearing in multiple crosswalk rows and _mu flags unique_IDs appearing in multiple crosswalk rows. In MATCHING/profile_names_score.do, lines 141-150 display these numbers in a markdown table under a records column labeled | ... dropped: record attached to >1 profile | and | ... dropped: profile attached to >1 record |.
findings.why_it_matters: A record linked to multiple profiles appears multiple times in the crosswalk, so count if _mh counts crosswalk rows rather than the number of unique records dropped. If a row has both _mh==1 and _mu==1, it is counted in both rows. The column is labeled records, but the reported numbers are non-additive row counts from an external crosswalk, misstating the volume of dropped census records.

findings.how_to_check: Tabulate the share of records dropped by Rule (3) across cells 0 through 4. Verify that in cell 1, the sum of Ancestry and FamilySearch agreement is forced to 100%.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain this only as an explicitly labeled sensitivity check illustrating the upper bound under the assumption that one source is always correct, and clarify in the text that it conditions on the outcome.
findings.title: Rule (3) robustness conditions sample inclusion on at least one source matching the reference
findings.what_the_code_does: Line 217 runs scoreblock "Rule (3): men, at least one source matches first name and surname" men full_last "(mf_anc & mlast_anc) | (mf_fs & mlast_fs) | (mf_ml & mlast_ml)". This restricts the sample to observations where at least one of the three transcription sources agrees with the profile reference.
findings.why_it_matters: Conditioning on the dependent variable (whether any transcription matches the reference) excludes records where all three transcriptions disagree with the profile. In cell 1 (where ML agrees with Ancestry and both disagree with FamilySearch), this condition guarantees that Ancestry agreement and FamilySearch agreement sum to exactly 100%, mechanically exaggerating agreement rates and distorting comparisons.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied (review/reports/2026-11-13_185429-working-prompt.md:18); claims-vs-code review was limited to statements and labels embedded in the uncommitted code and revision notes.

External census datasets, crosswalks, IPUMS extracts, and approximately 200 GB of profile scrapes (under E:/multigen_CM/DATA/INTERMEDIATE and $REP_SNU) reside outside the repository and are gitignored, so sample sizes, conflict frequencies, and numerical attrition could not be verified by execution.
The Stata pipeline was not runnable in this environment; all findings and verified items reflect static analysis of the source code.
Review was restricted to the uncommitted working-tree changes (MATCHING/profile_names_build.do, MATCHING/profile_names_score.do, and review/revision-notes-2026-11-13.md).
summary: The uncommitted scripts construct a detailed 1940 census-to-FamilySearch profile name benchmark with careful string normalization, deterministic tie-breaking, and cell partitioning. However, FamilySearch profile names are an endogenous genealogical benchmark that cannot independently validate transcription accuracy, and the analysis remains isolated from the replication pipeline with an unconfigured E: drive dependency. The single most important fix is to frame this exhibit strictly as agreement with a selected genealogical reference while integrating the build and score scripts into replication/config.do and replication/run_machineA.do.
